title: Claude Code: 2026 Feature Updates
content:
## Overview

Claude Code received substantial new capabilities in 2026, including Dynamic Workflows, enhanced background agent infrastructure, a unified Skills and slash commands system, and significant rate limit increases for developers. These additions shift Claude Code from a capable coding assistant into a platform for large-scale, parallel agentic automation.

---

## Dynamic Workflows

Introduced alongside Claude Opus 4.8 on May 28, 2026, **Dynamic Workflows** is Claude Code's most powerful automation feature to date. A single natural language instruction is decomposed into tens or hundreds of background subagents that run in parallel on a shared filesystem.

Unlike a standard agentic session where Claude works sequentially, Dynamic Workflows enables true parallelism at scale — a task like "migrate this codebase from Python 2 to Python 3" becomes a coordinated effort across dozens of specialized subagents, each handling a subset of files simultaneously.

Dynamic Workflows launched in research preview. It is compute-intensive; usage is tracked against your organization's rate limits.

---

## Background Agents and `.claude/agents/`

Claude Code supports **specialized background agents** defined as Markdown files in `.claude/agents/`. Each file specifies a system prompt, tool access list, and model selection:

```markdown
---
name: test-runner
description: Runs tests and interprets failures
model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
tools: Bash, Read
---
You are a specialized test runner. When given a file path, run the relevant tests, interpret failures, and return a structured report of pass/fail counts and root causes.
```

Agents are spawned by the coordinator via the `Agent` tool. Multiple agents can run concurrently. Agent files use kebab-case naming (`test-runner.md`, `code-reviewer.md`) — the filename becomes the label used when spawning.

**When to use background agents vs. inline subagents:** Use `.claude/agents/` definitions when the same specialized role recurs across sessions (e.g., a dedicated linter or test runner). Use inline `Agent` tool calls for one-off delegation within a task.

---

## Unified Skills and Slash Commands

Prior to 2026, Claude Code had two overlapping systems: **custom slash commands** (Markdown files in `.claude/commands/`) and **skills** (a newer structured system). These were unified in early 2026 — both approaches now create a `/command-name` entry and use the same format.

Skills follow the **Agent Skills open standard**, making them portable across Claude Code, Cursor, and other compatible tools. Claude Code ships with 60+ built-in commands and 5 bundled skills.

Key built-in commands added in 2026:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/goal` | Set a persistent session goal — Claude tracks it across all turns |
| `/agents` | List available background agents defined in this project |
| `/loop` | Run a command on a recurring interval within the session |

**The `/goal` command** has become widely adopted for long-horizon agentic tasks. Setting a goal gives Claude a reference point to check intermediate outputs against, reducing drift in multi-step operations.

Custom skills are stored at `.claude/skills/<skill-name>.md` (or `.claude/commands/<command-name>.md` — both paths work). The file becomes a slash command invokable as `/<skill-name>`.

---

## Effort Parameter

The API and claude.ai both support an **effort parameter** allowing callers to trade off speed against capability. Users on claude.ai can now explicitly control the effort Claude puts into a task; API callers pass it as a top-level request parameter.

Higher effort increases the depth of reasoning and the number of tool calls Claude will attempt before responding. Lower effort reduces latency and cost for straightforward tasks.

---

## Rate Limit Increases

Anthropic doubled rate limits on Claude Code and raised API limits for Claude Opus in 2026 to support production-scale agentic workloads. Organizations running Dynamic Workflows or large multi-agent pipelines had frequently hit the prior limits.

Current limits for your tier are visible in the [Anthropic Console](https://console.anthropic.com) under Settings → Rate Limits. A new **Rate Limits API** allows administrators to query limits programmatically:

```bash
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/rate-limits \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

---

## Dreaming (Managed Agents)

For developers building managed agent systems via the Claude API, **Dreaming** is a scheduled background process that reviews past sessions, surfaces recurring patterns, and writes curated memories to a store the agent reads at session start. Agents using Dreaming improve between runs without explicit retraining.

This is distinct from Claude Code's built-in `/memory` command, which edits the per-project `CLAUDE.md` memory file manually.
